user.title: Carnet scolaire
user.description:
![Carnet scolaire]({logo})

Which platform does your child's school use? Choose the one you log in to for the timetable, homework and grades.

pronote.title: PRONOTE
pronote.description: Choose how to connect. The QR code from the PRONOTE mobile app is the most reliable method: it enrols this Home Assistant as a device and avoids storing your password.

menu_options.qr_code: QR code from the mobile app (recommended)

reconfigure.title: Change the PRONOTE connection
reconfigure.description:
This entry connects to {url}. Choose how it should connect from now on -- the same method to correct the address, the username or the portal, or another one. The next form asks for the password or the QR code again: neither is shown back.

The new details are tried once before anything is saved, and must open this same account. The children you follow, the options and the history are kept.

menu_options.qr_code: QR code from the mobile app (recommended)

qr_code.title: Enrol with a QR code
qr_code.description:
In the PRONOTE mobile app, open the account menu and generate a QR code, choosing a four-digit code when asked.

The app draws the QR code as a picture, and the field below wants the JSON it encodes. So scan it with a QR code reader — your phone's camera or any scanner app — and share or copy the text it gives you, then paste that text below with the same four-digit code.

A QR code is single-use **and expires within minutes**, so the order matters: open this form first, generate the QR code second, and submit straight away. Generate a new one if this attempt fails -- the old one is spent either way.

data.account_pin: Two-factor PIN (if your account uses one)

data_description.qr_payload: The text a QR code reader returns when it scans the code the app draws: a JSON object with login, jeton and url. Paste it whole, not a photo or a link to the picture.
data_description.device_name: The name PRONOTE shows for this Home Assistant in the list of devices connected to the account -- only there. It does not name the device in Home Assistant, which takes the pupil's name from PRONOTE.
data_description.qr_pin: The one you chose in the app while generating the QR code. Not the account PIN below -- both are four digits, and they are different codes.
data_description.account_pin: The two-factor PIN set on the PRONOTE account itself, if it has one. Also four digits, and not the code above. Used for this login only and never stored. You will be asked for it again if PRONOTE requires it.

credentials.title: Username and password
credentials.description: Enter the address of your establishment's PRONOTE space, ending in eleve.html or parent.html.

data.account_pin: Two-factor PIN (if your account uses one)

data_description.pronote_url: The address of the establishment's PRONOTE page as your browser shows it, ending in parent.html for a parent account or eleve.html for a pupil's. Anything after .html is dropped before it is stored.
data_description.username: The username typed on the PRONOTE login page itself -- not the one of a regional portal (ENT).
data_description.password: The PRONOTE password of that account. It is stored, since this method has no other way to log in again; the QR code method avoids that.
data_description.account_pin: Used for this login only and never stored. You will be asked for it again if PRONOTE requires it.

ent.title: Federated login
ent.description: Select your regional education portal. Your credentials are the ones for that portal, not for PRONOTE itself.

data_description.pronote_url: The address of the establishment's PRONOTE page, ending in parent.html or eleve.html: the page the portal opens once you are logged in, not the portal's own address.
data_description.username: The username typed on the regional portal (ENT), not a PRONOTE one.
data_description.password: The password of that portal account. It is stored, since a federated login goes through the portal again every time.
data_description.ent: The portal your establishment signs you in through. Pick it from the list rather than typing a name: an unknown name is refused.

ecoledirecte.title: Connect to EcoleDirecte
ecoledirecte.description: Enter the credentials used to sign in to EcoleDirecte. The password is stored because EcoleDirecte does not issue a durable device token.

data_description.username: The username typed on the EcoleDirecte login page, for a parent or a pupil account.
data_description.password: The EcoleDirecte password of that account. It is stored, since EcoleDirecte issues no durable device token.

ecoledirecte_qcm.title: EcoleDirecte security question
ecoledirecte_qcm.description:
EcoleDirecte asks: {question}

Select the remembered answer. No account is created until the login succeeds.

data_description.choice: The answer EcoleDirecte expects for this account, as its own site asks it on a new device. It is remembered, so the question is not asked at every login.

children.title: Which children to follow
children.description: Each child you follow multiplies the number of daily requests to the server, so select only the ones you want.

data_description.children: Each ticked child gets its own device and entities. Untick a child you do not need: every child adds the same number of requests a day.

reauth_confirm.title: Reconnect to PRONOTE
reauth_confirm.description: The connection to {url} was refused. Enter a corrected password, or the two-factor PIN PRONOTE is asking for. The PIN is used once and never stored.

data_description.password: Leave empty to keep the stored password, for instance when PRONOTE is only asking for the two-factor PIN.
data_description.account_pin: The two-factor PIN set on the PRONOTE account, when PRONOTE asks for it. Used for this login only and never stored.

reauth_qr.title: Reconnect with a new QR code
reauth_qr.description:
The connection to {url} was refused. This account was enrolled from a QR code, so it has no password to correct: PRONOTE issues a new access token at every login, and once the stored one is refused the only way back in is a new QR code.

In the PRONOTE mobile app, generate a fresh QR code, choosing a four-digit code when asked, then paste its content below. Nothing else about this account changes -- the children you follow, your settings and your history are all kept.

data.account_pin: Two-factor PIN (if your account uses one)

data_description.qr_payload: The text a QR code reader returns when it scans the code the app draws: a JSON object with login, jeton and url. Paste it whole, not a photo or a link to the picture.
data_description.device_name: The name PRONOTE shows for this Home Assistant in the list of devices connected to the account -- only there. It does not name the device in Home Assistant, which takes the pupil's name from PRONOTE.
data_description.qr_pin: The one you chose in the app while generating the QR code. Not the account PIN below -- both are four digits, and they are different codes.
data_description.account_pin: The two-factor PIN set on the PRONOTE account itself, if it has one. Also four digits, and not the code above. Used for this login only and never stored. You will be asked for it again if PRONOTE requires it.

error.invalid_auth: PRONOTE refused these credentials. Repeatedly retrying a wrong password is what gets an address blocked, so check them before trying again.
error.mfa_required: PRONOTE is asking for the two-factor PIN of this account. Enter it above.
error.bootstrap_failed: The address answered, but did not return a PRONOTE session page. Check the address, and that the space is open right now.
error.ent_required: This establishment does not allow direct login to PRONOTE: the address leads to its ENT portal's own login page. Nothing was sent and your password was not refused. Go back to the login methods and choose “Federated login (ENT)”, with the portal's username and password -- or the app's QR code, if the establishment has enabled it.
error.invalid_qr: The QR code or its four-digit code was refused. A QR code can only be used once, so generate a new one in the app.
error.qr_refused: PRONOTE would not honour this QR code. Its four-digit code was right -- a wrong one is reported separately, and is caught before anything is sent -- so what was refused is the QR code itself. Almost always that means it has already been used, or was generated more than a few minutes ago: PRONOTE issues them for single use and expires them quickly. Generate a new one and use it straight away, with the form already open. If a QR code you generated seconds earlier is refused too, the account may not be allowed to enrol a new device -- check with the establishment rather than retrying, because repeatedly retrying a refused login is what gets an address blocked.
error.invalid_qr_payload: That does not look like the content of a PRONOTE QR code. It should be a JSON object with login, jeton and url -- the first two written in hexadecimal. Paste it whole, exactly as the app gives it.
error.unknown_ent: No ENT provider by that name is installed. Pick one from the list rather than typing it in: an unrecognised name does not fall back to anything sensible, it sends this portal's username and password to the PRONOTE server instead.
error.invalid_qcm: Select one of the proposed answers.
error.ed_invalid_auth: EcoleDirecte refused these credentials. Check them before trying again.
error.rate_limited: Too many login attempts in the last hour, so this one was not sent. Wait a little before trying again: repeatedly retrying a login is what gets an address blocked.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. Check the Home Assistant log.

abort.reconfigure_successful: Connection updated. The entry is reloading with it; its devices, entities, history and options are unchanged.
abort.reconfigure_wrong_account: These details sign in to a different account from the one this entry follows, so nothing was changed: applying them would have pointed this entry at somebody else's child while keeping this child's name and history. Use the details of this entry's own account, or add the other account separately.
abort.wrong_account: That QR code belongs to a different PRONOTE account, so it was not applied: reconnecting this one with it would have pointed it at somebody else's child while keeping this child's name and history. Generate a QR code from the account this entry follows, or add the other account separately.

error.invalid_timezone: Not a timezone this system knows. It is written Region/City -- Europe/Paris, not Paris -- and it has to match the zone database exactly. Leave the box empty to follow Home Assistant's own timezone.

init.title: PRONOTE options
init.description: Currently about **{estimate} requests a day** for {students} child(ren). Measured session lifetime: {measured} min.

general.title: General
general.description: Currently about **{estimate} requests a day** for {students} child(ren). Measured session lifetime: {measured} min.

data_description.master_tick: How often the integration checks which tiers are due. Not how often it calls PRONOTE.
data_description.homework_horizon: How many days of homework to display. This does not change the number of requests: PRONOTE returns a week range either way.
data_description.wake_margin: Minutes subtracted from the first lesson of the day to produce the wake-up sensor.
data_description.stale_after: Multiples of a tier's interval after which its entities are marked stale. They keep their last value rather than going unavailable, because an entity that flickers unavailable fires automations spuriously.
data_description.establishment_timezone: PRONOTE returns local times with no timezone. This is the timezone they are interpreted in. Leave it empty to follow Home Assistant's own timezone, which is what you want unless the establishment is in a different one from you. Written as Region/City, for example Europe/Paris.
data_description.session_strategy: Whether to keep one session alive between collections (lazy) or open a new one for each batch. Lazy starts cautious and switches by itself if the server turns out to expire sessions quickly, so it is never worse than the alternative.
data_description.write_operations_enabled: On for a new installation. When on, ticking a homework item, marking news read and sending messages are possible, and the establishment sees those actions.

tiers.title: Collection intervals
tiers.description:
Currently about **{estimate} requests a day** for {students} child(ren). Measured session lifetime: {measured} min.

One interval per category. The estimate above updates when you save.

data_description.interval_timetable: Minutes between two collections of this category. Shorter means fresher data and more requests a day.
data_description.enabled_timetable: Off stops collecting this category altogether and saves its requests; its entities stay unavailable.
data_description.interval_homework: Minutes between two collections of this category. Shorter means fresher data and more requests a day.

rate_limit.title: Rate limiting
rate_limit.description:
Currently about **{estimate} requests a day** for {students} child(ren). Measured session lifetime: {measured} min.

These defaults were chosen to stay well inside what a PRONOTE server tolerates. Raising them raises the risk of a sanction, which is borne by the account, not by the integration.

data.bootstrap_hold: Pause when the session page is unreadable

data_description.min_request_interval: Spacing applied to every request, so a batch never arrives as a burst.
data_description.max_requests_per_hour: The sustained rate the token bucket refills at.
data_description.burst_size: How many requests may go out back to back before the hourly rate applies.
data_description.max_requests_per_day: Hard ceiling. Low-priority tiers stop being served well before it is reached, so the cap protects the account rather than surprising you.
data_description.max_wait: If a tier would have to wait longer than this for its budget, it is postponed instead. Its entities keep their values.
data_description.max_logins_per_day: A login costs about five requests, so this is counted separately.
data_description.max_failed_logins_per_hour: The single most important setting here. PRONOTE sanctions repeated failed logins by blocking the address, and that sanction is undocumented and costly. Keep this low.
data_description.credentials_hold: How long to stop trying once the failed-login limit is reached. A manual reconnection clears it immediately.
data_description.bootstrap_hold: Applied when the address answers without a PRONOTE session page. The cause is not knowable from the response, so no cause is claimed.
data_description.backoff_base: First wait after a server error. It doubles at each consecutive failure, with jitter.
data_description.connect_timeout: The upstream library sets no timeout at all, so this is applied by this integration.
data_description.read_timeout: How long to wait for a response before abandoning a request.
data_description.quiet_hours_enabled: Stop collecting overnight. Roughly a third of the daily budget, spent on data nobody reads while asleep.
data_description.quiet_start: When scheduled collection pauses each evening. A button press, a service call and the refill after a restart still go through.
data_description.quiet_end: When scheduled collection resumes in the morning.

state.lesson_restored: A cancelled lesson is back on

refresh.name: Refresh
refresh.description: Asks the scheduler for a priority pass. Does not bypass the rate limiter, so pressing it repeatedly costs one batch, not several.

tiers.name: Tiers
tiers.description: Which categories to refresh. All of them if left empty.

get_ical_url.name: Get the iCal URL
get_ical_url.description: Returns the timetable subscription URL in the response. It is never stored in a state or an attribute: anyone holding this URL can read the child's timetable without a password.

get_identity.name: Get the identity
get_identity.description: Returns the personal details and legal guardians in the response. Never stored in a state.

mark_homework_done.name: Tick a homework item
mark_homework_done.description: Marks one homework item done or not done. The establishment sees this. Requires writing to be enabled in the options.

homework_id.name: Homework identifier
homework_id.description: Taken from the id field of the homework sensor's items.

mark_information_read.name: Mark a news item read
mark_information_read.description: Marks one news item as read. Requires writing to be enabled.

information_id.name: News identifier
information_id.description: Taken from the id field of the news sensor's items.

send_message.name: Send a message
send_message.description: Replies to an existing discussion, or starts a new one with named recipients. Give either a discussion identifier or a list of recipients, not both. Requires writing to be enabled.

discussion_id.name: Discussion identifier
discussion_id.description: To reply to an existing thread.

subject.name: Subject
subject.description: Required when starting a new discussion.

recipients.name: Recipients
recipients.description: Names as PRONOTE publishes them. An unmatched name is refused rather than silently dropped.

generate_timetable_pdf.name: Generate a timetable PDF
generate_timetable_pdf.description: Asks PRONOTE to render a PDF and returns its URL in the response.

get_rate_limit_status.name: Get the rate limiter status
get_rate_limit_status.description: Returns the full budget and scheduler state in the response. Costs no request: it reads counters already in memory.

get_attachment_url.name: Get an attachment's address
get_attachment_url.description: Returns, in the response, a short-lived address that opens one homework file. Costs no request: the document is fetched only when the address is opened.

key.name: Attachment key
key.description: The key of an entry in the attachment_refs attribute.

writes_disabled.message: Writing to PRONOTE is disabled. Turn on “Allow writing to PRONOTE” in the integration options first.

service_deferred.message: Postponed by the rate limiter ({reason}). Try again in about {seconds} seconds.

device_not_pronote.message: Device {device_id} does not belong to a PRONOTE account.

student_required.message: This account follows several children ({children}). Target the child's device rather than the account.

attachment_not_collected.message: Homework has not been collected for this child yet. Try again in a moment.

attachment_unknown.message: No homework file with this key is known for this child. Refresh the dashboard: the homework may have changed.

subject_required.message: A subject is required to start a new discussion.

discussion_not_found.message: No discussion with identifier {discussion_id} is visible to this account.

discussion_closed.message: Discussion {discussion_id} is closed and cannot be replied to.

todo_item_unknown.message: That to-do item has no PRONOTE identifier, so it cannot be updated.

homework_tick_parent_account.message: PRONOTE does not record a homework tick sent from a parent account: only the student's own account can tick homework. Nothing was sent.

write_not_applied.message: PRONOTE accepted the request but did not record it: the item read back unchanged. Try again later, or make the change in PRONOTE itself.

item_not_found.message: That item is no longer on PRONOTE as it was last read: it was withdrawn or changed since. Nothing was sent. Refresh, then try again.

service_login_refused.message: PRONOTE was not contacted: the rate limiter is holding back logins ({reason}). Nothing was sent. Try again later; retrying sooner makes it last longer.

service_reauth_required.message: PRONOTE refused the account's credentials, or asked for the two-factor PIN. Re-authenticate the integration from its page in Settings, then try again.

service_unreachable.message: PRONOTE could not be reached, or did not answer in time. The request may not have been received. Try again in a few minutes.

service_refused.message: PRONOTE refused the request. The integration is backing off; try again later.

service_unreadable.message: PRONOTE answered, but the answer could not be read. This usually means the establishment's PRONOTE changed; please report it with the integration's diagnostics.

service_internal_error.message: The request could not be completed because of a fault in this integration. The Home Assistant log says more; please report it.

service_not_supported.message: The {source} source does not support the {service} action.

homework_tick_not_supported.message: The {source} source does not support ticking homework.

todo_item_owned_by_pronote.message: Only the tick can be changed. The subject, the wording and the due date of a homework item belong to the teacher, in PRONOTE.

setup_auth_failed.message: The school platform refused the saved login, or asks for a confirmation [{error_type}]. Re-authenticate the integration.

setup_unreachable.message: The school platform's login page could not be read [{error_type}]. The integration will try again.

setup_login_postponed.message: The login was refused or postponed [{error_type}]. The integration will try again.

setup_unreadable.message: The school platform answered with data this integration cannot read [{error_type}]. The integration will try again.

setup_server_refused.message: The school platform refused the request [{error_type}]. The integration will try again.

setup_network_error.message: The school platform could not be reached [{error_type}]. The integration will try again.

condition_entity_missing.message: There is no {key} entity on device {device_id}: this establishment does not publish the data this condition reads.

trigger_device_not_followed.message: Device {device_id} is not a child this account currently follows, so this trigger can never fire. Select the device again in the automation, or delete the stale one.

account_unreadable.title: PRONOTE answered something this integration cannot read
account_unreadable.description: The address {url} and the credentials are both fine: PRONOTE answered, and the answer is outside what the pinned pronotepy version can decode. This usually means the establishment's PRONOTE changed something. There is nothing to correct on your side -- please report it, ideally with the integration's diagnostics attached.

invalid_credentials.title: PRONOTE credentials refused
invalid_credentials.description: PRONOTE refused the credentials {attempts} times, so attempts have been paused until {until}. Repeatedly retrying a wrong password is what gets an address blocked. Reconfigure the integration to enter corrected credentials.

bootstrap_failed.title: Cannot read the PRONOTE session page
bootstrap_failed.description: {url} answered, but the response contained no PRONOTE session block. This can mean the address is wrong, the space is closed for maintenance, the establishment changed its URL, or the server is returning an error page. The response does not say which, so no cause is claimed here. Retrying automatically until {until}.

daily_cap_near.title: Approaching the daily request limit
daily_cap_near.description: {calls} of {cap} requests used today. Low-priority categories are already being postponed. Lengthening the intervals of the categories you care least about in the options is the usual fix.

mfa_required.title: PRONOTE is asking for the two-factor PIN
mfa_required.description: This integration deliberately never stores the two-factor PIN, so it has to be entered again. Reconfigure the integration to supply it.

trigger_type.lesson_restored: A cancelled lesson is back on

condition_type.is_not_school_day: It is not a school day
condition_type.is_not_in_class: The child is not in class
